summary:
The fixed execution decided all three comparisons, so the stranded-leader verification question is closed with a measured interpretation and a promoted fact (valid:true).

Receipt 32b2614b51cd4e06a91be66d8bed1c4b (completed, exit 0) shows the protection holding. Index 0 verify_control_start records the leader server-ea62e7ff in state Leader with the 300ms lease; index 1 verify_healthy reports error_empty true in 0ms with the node still Leader, so comparison 0 holds — a healthy verification succeeds immediately. Index 2 verify_probe_start records the same node still in Leader while isolated (peers_connected 0); index 3 verify_partitioned reports completed true in 306ms, error_empty false with "leadership lost while committing log", state Follower and the 6s client wait limit, so comparison 1 holds (bounded completion, no hang) and comparison 2 holds (the stranded request fails instead of claiming success). The source accounts for the endpoint: VerifyLeader counts only peer replies (api.go:883-893), silence is resolved by the leader loop's lease check stepping down when fewer than quorumSize voters were contacted within LeaderLeaseTimeout (raft.go:1036-1081), and the step-down cleanup answers pending verifications with ErrLeadershipLost — exactly the observed error text; the configuration also requires the lease not to exceed the heartbeat timeout (config.go:333-376), which is recorded as the reason the probe uses a 1:1 ratio.

Conclusion recorded as holds with the boundaries kept explicit: one 1:1 timeout configuration, isolation rather than a crash, the followers' concurrent election outside the measured endpoint, and a single unloaded in-process observation, so no upper bound under load is claimed. A fact was promoted with executions at indices 0-3, and the investigation is marked explained. The run also corroborates the earlier reading that a late replication notification cannot double-complete a verification future, since this node had already answered and left the leader state.
